learn.hook: A balloon and a whistle! How much money do you need for both?
points: We add rupees just like numbers.
Add the notes first. Then add the coins.
Count on for ₹10 notes: ₹50, ₹60, ₹70.

example.q: Aisha has a ₹50 note, a ₹20 note and a ₹5 coin. How much money is that?

learn.reallife: At the fair we add the prices of rides and snacks to see how much to pay.

quiz.q: A balloon costs ₹15. A whistle costs ₹10. How much for both?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Kabir has a ₹50 note and a ₹20 note. How much money does he have?
quiz.explain: ₹50 + ₹20: 5 tens and 2 tens make 7 tens. That is ₹70.
quiz.mistake: Writes 50 and 20 side by side, or takes away

quiz.q: What is ₹45 + ₹27?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the new ten

quiz.q: Harpreet buys a toffee for ₹2, a pencil for ₹5 and a pen for ₹10. How much does she pay?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one of the three things

quiz.q: Joseph has three ₹10 coins and four ₹1 coins. How much money does he have?
quiz.explain: Three ₹10 coins make ₹30. Four ₹1 coins make ₹4. ₹30 + ₹4 = ₹34.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of coins, or swaps tens and ones

quiz.q: Riya saves ₹20 on Monday and ₹20 on Tuesday. How much does she save in all?
quiz.explain: ₹20 + ₹20: 2 tens and 2 tens make 4 tens. That is ₹40.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

teach.ask: Gappu: I have ₹50 and ₹20. How much money is that?
teach.praise: Super! Add them up: ₹50 and ₹20 make ₹70!
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away? What do ₹50 and ₹20 make together?

revise.summary: We add rupees just like numbers, like ₹20 + ₹15 = ₹35. Add the notes first, then add the coins.
focus: Find how much money from notes and coins.
Add two or three prices.
Add money with carrying.
remember: Add the notes first. Then add the coins.
traps: Don't take away when finding the total.
Don't forget to carry the new ten: ₹45 + ₹27 = ₹72.
Don't leave out one of the things.

topics.title: Money for rides at the fair

learn.hook: The fair is here! Giant wheel, merry-go-round ... How much money do you need?
points: To find the money needed, add the prices of all the things.
Money spent = money we had - money left.
If Ria had ₹40 and has ₹37 left, she spent ₹3.
'₹14 more than ₹43' means add: ₹43 + ₹14 = ₹57.

example.q: Raju had ₹40. After a ride he has ₹37 left. How much did the ride cost?
steps: Money spent = money he had - money left.

learn.reallife: At a mela, check the prices before you choose a ride.

quiz.q: Raju had ₹40. After a ride, he has ₹37 left. How much did the ride cost?
quiz.mistake: Adds the money he had and the money left

quiz.q: A toy train ride costs ₹15 and a balloon costs ₹5. How much money is needed for both?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Gita has ₹43. Her mother gives her ₹14 more. How much does she have now?
quiz.mistake: Takes away when the word 'more' is used

quiz.q: Leela had ₹50. She has ₹18 left after the fair. How much did she spend?
quiz.explain: Spent = 50 - 18. Break a ten: 10 - 8 = 2, tens 4 - 1 = 3. So ₹32.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: Candy floss costs ₹12 more than a ₹20 ride. What does the candy floss cost?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Sam wants a ₹25 ride and a ₹10 snack. How much money does he need?
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

teach.ask: Gappu: I had ₹40 and now I have ₹37. How much did I spend?
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away to find what I spent?

revise.summary: To find the money needed, add the prices of all the things. Money spent = money we had - money left.
focus: Find the money needed for rides and snacks.
Find money spent from money had and money left.
Solve 'more than' money stories.
remember: Money spent = money we had - money left.
traps: Don't add the money had and the money left. Take away.
'More' means add, not take away.
Find the total, not the difference, for money needed.

learn.hook: The fair is here! But first, let's get to know our money.
points: Indian money is the rupee. We write it as ₹.
Notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100 and more.
Small coins can add up to a bigger amount. Two ₹5 coins make ₹10.

steps: We said 5 numbers. That is 5 coins.

learn.reallife: At the shop we pay with coins and notes. Your piggy bank is full of coins!

quiz.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹10?
quiz.explain: Each coin is ₹1. Count 1 to 10. That is 10 coins.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one coin is enough for any amount

quiz.q: Riya has two ₹10 notes and one ₹5 coin. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one ₹10 note, or forgets the coin

quiz.q: How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s till 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of a coin instead of the number of coins

quiz.q: Which is the most money?
steps: The ₹50 note is the most money.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a coin is worth more because it is heavy

quiz.q: Arjun has one ₹50 note. Kabir has five ₹10 notes. Who has more money?
quiz.explain: Five ₹10 notes: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is ₹50, same as Arjun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more notes always means more money

quiz.q: Meena has three ₹20 notes. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 20 instead of counting three ₹20 notes

teach.ask: Gappu: How many ₹2 coins do I need to make ₹10?
teach.praise: Yes! Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Five ₹2 coins make ₹10!
teach.nudge: Can I count by 2s up to 10? How many coins is that?

revise.summary: Indian money is the rupee, written as ₹, and we use coins and notes. Small coins can add up to a bigger amount, like two ₹5 coins make ₹10.
focus: Know the coins and notes we use.
Find how many coins make an amount.
Find the total of some notes and coins.
traps: More notes do not always mean more money.
Don't give the value of a coin when the number of coins is asked.
Don't add 3 and 20 for three ₹20 notes.

topics.title: A closer look at our notes

learn.hook: Look closely at a ₹500 note. What can you see?
points: Every note shows its amount in numbers, like 500.
It also shows the amount in words, like 'Five Hundred Rupees'.
Mahatma Gandhi's picture is on the front of our notes.
The back shows a famous place. The Red Fort is on the ₹500 note.
The ₹10 note shows the Konark Sun Temple and the ₹100 note shows Rani ki Vav.
learn.reallife: On Independence Day, the Prime Minister speaks at the Red Fort, the place on the ₹500 note.

items.text: The Red Fort is on the ₹___ note

quiz.q: Which monument is on the back of the ₹500 note?
quiz.explain: The ₹500 note shows the Red Fort in Delhi.
steps: Each note has a picture on the back.
The ₹500 note shows the Red Fort in Delhi.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a famous monument without looking

quiz.q: How is 500 written in words on the note?
quiz.explain: 500 is five hundreds, so it is Five Hundred Rupees.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fifty and five hundred

quiz.q: A note says 'One Hundred Rupees'. How much is it in numbers?
quiz.mistake: Writes too few or too many zeros

quiz.q: Whose picture is on the front of Indian notes?
quiz.explain: Gandhiji's picture is on the front of our notes.
steps: The front of our notes has a picture of a person.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the national animal or bird is on the front

quiz.q: Ravi sees 'Twenty Rupees' on a note. How much is the note?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up twenty and twelve

quiz.q: Which is worth more: a ₹500 note or a ₹200 note?
quiz.mistake: Compares the size of the paper, not the amount

teach.ask: Gappu: What do I see on a ₹500 note?
teach.praise: Great looking! 500 in numbers and words, Gandhiji in front and the Red Fort at the back.
teach.nudge: How is the amount shown? What picture is on the back?

revise.summary: Every note shows its amount in numbers and in words, with Mahatma Gandhi's picture on the front. The back shows a famous place, like the Red Fort on the ₹500 note.
focus: Read the amount in numbers and words.
Know whose picture is on the front.
Know the places on the ₹10, ₹100 and ₹500 notes.
remember: Mahatma Gandhi's picture is on the front of our notes.
₹500: Red Fort. ₹10: Konark Sun Temple. ₹100: Rani ki Vav.
traps: Don't mix up fifty and five hundred.
Don't mix up twenty and twelve.
Compare the amount, not the size of the paper.

learn.hook: Nanaji bought toffees with paise long ago! What is a paisa?
points: 1 rupee = 100 paise.
A 50-paise coin is half a rupee. Two of them make ₹1.
Four 25-paise coins make 1 rupee: 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = 100.
Five 20-paise coins make 1 rupee: 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 100.
learn.reallife: Old 25-paise and 20-paise coins can be found in coin collections.

games.title: True or false?
items: 1 rupee = 100 paise
100 paise make one rupee.
Four 25-paise coins make 1 rupee
Five 20-paise coins make 50 paise
They make 100 paise, which is ₹1.
Two 50-paise coins make 1 rupee
10 paise is more than 1 rupee
1 rupee is 100 paise, much more than 10 paise.

quiz.q: How many paise make 1 rupee?
quiz.mistake: Thinks 10 paise make a rupee

quiz.q: How many 25-paise coins make 1 rupee?
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of one coin

quiz.q: How many 20-paise coins make 1 rupee?
quiz.mistake: Stops at 80 paise

quiz.q: Dadi has three 25-paise coins. How many paise is that?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 25

quiz.q: Which coins make exactly 1 rupee?
quiz.mistake: Thinks four 20-paise coins make a rupee

quiz.q: Two 50-paise coins make how many paise?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one coin

teach.ask: Gappu: How many paise are in one rupee?
teach.nudge: How many paise do I need for one whole rupee?

revise.summary: 1 rupee = 100 paise. Two 50-paise coins, four 25-paise coins or five 20-paise coins make 1 rupee.
focus: Know how many paise make a rupee.
Find how many paise coins make ₹1.
Add paise coins.
remember: Four 25-paise coins make ₹1. Five 20-paise coins make ₹1.
traps: 10 paise do not make a rupee. 100 paise do.
Four 20-paise coins make only 80 paise.
Don't add 3 and 25 for three 25-paise coins.

learn.hook: Pop a balloon, win money! Each balloon has an amount written on it.
points: Add the amounts on all the balloons you pop to find your total.
To make a given amount, choose balloons that add up to it.
To win the most, pop the balloons with the biggest amounts.
Check your choice by adding again.

example.q: Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. With 3 chances, how can you win the most?

learn.reallife: At a school fun fair, games give small prizes for points.

quiz.q: Tara pops balloons with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2. How much does she win?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one balloon

quiz.q: Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. Which two make ₹25?
quiz.mistake: Does not add to check

quiz.q: Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. With 3 chances, what is the most you can win?
steps: To win the most, pop the 3 biggest.
quiz.mistake: Adds all five balloons

quiz.q: Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. With 4 chances, what is the most you can win?
quiz.mistake: Uses only 3 chances or all 5

quiz.q: Arun wants to win exactly ₹12. Which balloons should he pop?
quiz.mistake: Does not add to check

quiz.q: Mina won ₹20 and ₹5. Her brother won ₹10, ₹10 and ₹2. Who won more?
quiz.mistake: Thinks more balloons means more money

teach.ask: Gappu: I get 3 chances. How do I win the most money?
teach.praise: Yes! Pop the three biggest balloons and add them.
teach.nudge: Which balloons should I pick to win the most?

revise.summary: In the balloon game, add the amounts on the balloons you pop to find your total. To win the most, pop the balloons with the biggest amounts.
focus: Add the amounts on popped balloons.
Choose balloons that make an exact amount.
Find the most you can win with some chances.
remember: To win the most, pop the biggest amounts.
Check your choice by adding again.
traps: Don't use more or fewer chances than you have.
More balloons do not always mean more money.
Don't leave out a balloon when adding.

learn.hook: ₹66 for a storybook. Which notes and coins will you give?
points: An amount can be made in many ways.
To use the fewest notes and coins, start with the biggest one that fits.
Keep taking the biggest that fits till the amount is made.

example.q: Pay ₹38 with the fewest notes and coins.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers try to give change with as few coins as they can.

games.title: True or false?
items: ₹66 can be made with ₹50, ₹10, ₹5 and ₹1
There is only one way to make ₹20
A ₹20 note, two ₹10s, four ₹5s and more.
To use the fewest notes, start with the biggest that fits
Big notes cover more of the amount.
Two ₹20 notes and one ₹10 note make ₹50

quiz.q: Which set makes ₹66?
quiz.mistake: Does not add all the notes and coins

quiz.q: Another way to make ₹66 is ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹5 + ___. What is missing?
quiz.mistake: Does not add the given notes first

quiz.q: What is the fewest number of notes and coins to pay ₹30?
quiz.explain: ₹20 + ₹10 = ₹30. That is 2 notes. There is no ₹30 note.
quiz.mistake: Uses three ₹10 notes

quiz.q: Which set pays ₹38 with the fewest notes and coins?
quiz.explain: All three make ₹38. The second set uses only 5 pieces; the other two use 6.
steps: The other two have 6 pieces. Answer: ₹20, ₹10, ₹5, ₹2, ₹1
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest note

quiz.q: Ria pays ₹45 with some ₹20 notes and one ₹5 coin. How many ₹20 notes does she use?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ₹5 coin

quiz.q: Which is the fewest notes to pay ₹150?
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest note

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to pay ₹38 with as few notes and coins as I can. How?
teach.praise: Yes! Start with the biggest that fits, ₹20, then ₹10, ₹5, ₹2, ₹1.
teach.nudge: Which note should I start with?

revise.summary: An amount can be made in many ways, like ₹66 = ₹50 + ₹10 + ₹5 + ₹1. To use the fewest notes and coins, keep taking the biggest one that fits.
focus: Check which set makes an amount.
Find a missing note or coin.
Pay with the fewest notes and coins.
remember: Fewest notes and coins: start with the biggest one that fits.
traps: Don't use three ₹10 notes for ₹30. ₹20 + ₹10 is fewer.
Add the given notes before finding what is missing.
Don't forget the ₹5 coin when working back.

learn.hook: You give the shopkeeper ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. Do you get money back?
points: The shopkeeper sells. We buy and pay.
If we pay more than the price, the shopkeeper gives money back. This is called change.
Change = money we give − price.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy: change is ₹5.

example.q: Meena buys a ribbon for ₹12. She pays with a ₹20 note. How much change does she get?

learn.reallife: At the fair, the vegetable market or the school canteen, we pay and get change.

games.title: True or false?
items: If you pay ₹10 for a ₹10 toffee packet, you get no change.
You paid the exact price. ₹10 − ₹10 = ₹0.
Paying ₹50 for a ₹30 book gives ₹20 change.
Paying ₹20 for a ₹14 pen gives ₹4 change.
With only ₹10 you can buy a toy that costs ₹25.
₹25 is more than ₹10. You need ₹15 more.
The shopkeeper gives change when we pay more than the price.
Change is the extra money given back.

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹15. Arjun pays ₹20. How much change does he get?
quiz.explain: Change = ₹20 − ₹15. Count up from 15 to 20: that is 5. So ₹5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the money and the price

quiz.q: Aisha has ₹30. A doll costs ₹25. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹30 is more than ₹25, so she can buy it. ₹30 − ₹25 = ₹5 change.
steps: Answer: Yes, and she gets ₹5 back
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the money with the price

quiz.q: Kabir pays ₹50 for a toy car that costs ₹35. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Does 5 − 0 in the ones instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹40. He buys a ball for ₹18. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 0 in the ones, or forgets that one ten was broken

quiz.q: A stall sells laddoos at ₹5 each. How much for 4 laddoos?
quiz.explain: 4 laddoos at ₹5 each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So ₹20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5 instead of counting ₹5 four times

quiz.q: Riya wants a ₹60 bag. She has ₹45. How much more money does she need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts, or does 5 − 0 in the ones

teach.ask: Gappu: I pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. How much change do I get?
teach.praise: Yes! ₹20 take away ₹15 is ₹5. I get ₹5 back!
teach.nudge: How much more is ₹20 than ₹15? Should I take away?

revise.summary: The shopkeeper sells and we buy and pay. If we pay more than the price, the money we get back is called change: change = money we give − price.
focus: Find the change.
Tell if there is enough money to buy something.
Find how much more money is needed.
remember: Pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy: change is ₹5.
traps: Don't add the money and the price to find change.
Don't do 5 − 0 in ₹50 − ₹35. Break a ten.
Don't add 4 and 5 for 4 laddoos at ₹5.
